description: Full-fidelity specification to rebuild the OCI Full BOM workbook from scratch. Customer-neutral: {{CUSTOMER}} is substituted at export time with the BOM name entered in the app.
rebuild_instructions: Rebuild with Python/openpyxl: (1) create workbook, one sheet per entry in "sheets" in order; (2) set tab_color, sheet view (showGridLines, zoomScale), freeze_panes, auto_filter; (3) apply column_dimensions (width/hidden; "range" [min,max] means apply to that column span) and row_dimensions (height/hidden); (4) apply merged_cells ranges FIRST, then write cells — openpyxl merge_cells() wipes styles already set inside a merged range, but styles assigned to MergedCell objects after merging serialize correctly; (5) write every cell in "cells": "v"=literal value, "f"=formula string (cached_value shows expected result), "s"=style id resolved via top-level "styles" registry (font/fill/border/alignment/number_format); entries with "merged":true are non-anchor merged cells — set style only, never value; (6) add conditional_formatting rules, data_validations, hyperlinks, comments; (7) insert images: decode base64 from "images" registry, anchor per "anchor" (col/row are 0-indexed, offsets in EMU, ext_emu is display size in EMU; 914400 EMU = 1 inch); (8) colors: {"rgb":"AARRGGBB"} or {"theme":N,"tint":T} resolved against workbook.theme_xml_base64; (9) values typed {"_type":"datetime","iso":...} must be converted back to Python datetime objects; (10) POST-PROCESS the saved xlsx zip: (a) replace xl/theme/theme1.xml with workbook.theme_xml_base64 decoded, (b) rewrite font id 0 in xl/styles.xml to workbook.default_font (Oracle Sans 10) so unstyled cells inherit the right typeface, (c) rows with height 0 in row_dimensions must get ht="0" customHeight="1" in the sheet XML (openpyxl drops zero heights).

C13.v: Pricing uses OCI flexible VM shapes, where OCPU and memory can be sized independently. Based on benchmark comparisons against {{CUSTOMER}}'s current Intel-based shapes and the state-of-the-art AMD E6 target, this BOM assumes a 20% performance-per-core improvement. The model applies that as a 20% reduction to the OCPU compute-price component only; OCPU count, RAM, and storage quantities are unchanged.

C14.v: Virtual rows use 2 vCPU = 1 OCPU for OCI planning. Rows labeled Physical use 1 physical core = 1 OCPU. The E6 optimization remains a compute-price adjustment only; it does not reduce the displayed OCPU count.

C16.v: Backup storage and the NAS/file-share estate remain outside the selected baseline until scoped. The Annexure Addendum to Storage includes scenario-based price modeling for these larger storage items, but those scenario rows are excluded from the final price unless explicitly marked for inclusion. OCI storage can be sized to actual required capacity by service and tier, so {{CUSTOMER}} does not need to overprovision storage up front and can pay for the capacity it chooses to use.
